A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuroMerging study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original NeuroMerging evaluations on NLP, vision, and LLaMA2 benchmarks, together with subspace ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations involving layer-wise AdaMerging combinations and projections.

M1.justification: Section 6.5 adds a hybrid configuration combining NeuroMerging with publicly shared layer-wise AdaMerging and AdaMerging++ coefficients. The standalone decomposition, SVD-based merging, and Algorithm 1 operations remain unchanged; the expanded SVD explanation documents an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven T5 training tasks, six held-out generalization tasks, three LLaMA2 benchmarks, and eight vision datasets. The added layer-wise experiments retain the existing vision tasks and model sizes.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds Consensus TA, Consensus TIES, and NPS to the LLaMA2 comparison, reporting averages of 33.5, 34.4, and 35.3. Tables 8 and 10 add layer-wise AdaMerging and AdaMerging++ comparisons; the earlier task-wise variants remain.

E3.justification: The new hybrid evaluations reuse publicly shared layer-wise coefficients. Figure 5 extends the displayed λ2 range from 6 to 8, although the written grid-search bounds remain unchanged. Section 5.4 replaces the account of fine-tuning the visual encoder with one of reusing shared Ilharco checkpoints; this revises the reported setup without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds hybrid compatibility tests, extends the vision subspace analysis to layer-wise methods, broadens Figure 5's sensitivity evidence, and introduces Appendix C.4's systematic analysis of task-level shortfalls. The masking-ratio and merging-function ablations already existed in v2 Appendices C.2 and C.1 and are relocated to the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the empirical comparisons. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark and efficiency scores are unchanged. New Table 8 reports, for example, layer-wise AdaMerging plus NeuroMerging at 82.3 versus 80.1 on ViT-B/32 and 91.3 versus 90.8 on ViT-L/14. Additional comparator and projection rows supply new results, while Figure 5 adds a performance decline at larger λ2 values. These are additions under the stated configurations, not improved standalone scores.

T1.justification: The neuronal subspace definitions, activation derivation, and Appendix B argument are retained. Appendix A.3 explicitly writes out the standard SVD, projection, and reconstruction algebra for the procedure already described in v2; it introduces no new theoretical assumption, proof, or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a neuronal interpretation of task vectors, complementary sensitivity/adaptation subspaces, training-free NeuroMerging, and strong NLP and vision performance. Terminology and tense changes do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.4 interprets task-specific weaknesses through possible semantic-information loss, cross-task representational shifts, and capacity mismatches, and discusses Fisher Merging's advantages on particular vision tasks. Section 6.5 hypothesizes that TIES can discard information useful to NeuroMerging. Section 6.3 adds practical advice to prioritize λ2 tuning; the existing formal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds SVD implementation details, Algorithm 1 explicitly lists its mask and projection inputs, and Section 5.4 identifies shared vision checkpoints. Appendix D revises reported NLP/CV hardware from A6000 GPUs with 48GB to GeForce 4090 GPUs with 24GB, retaining A6000 hardware for LLMs. The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a project link; its contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Du et al. (2025), Neural Parameter Search, removes Raia (2021), and expands discussion of compatibility with AdaMerging. The central neuron-level novelty positioning remains unchanged. Most other reference changes update bibliographic details for retained works.

P1.justification: v3 edits tense and terminology, expands the framework caption and SVD explanation, reorganizes Appendix A, and promotes two appendix analyses into Section 6. Author affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable, although Appendix A.2 introduces a malformed masking-definition sentence containing only 't' where v2 supplied the formula.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains panel labels and a revised caption, Figure 5 is extended, Table 8 is new, and the LLaMA2 and vision-projection tables gain rows. The granularity table and existing ablation displays move into the main text. Most figures and table designs are retained, with local resizing, caption edits, and reflow.

improvement.justification: The added layer-wise comparisons and explicit task-level failure analysis make the evaluation more informative, while the SVD and checkpoint disclosures improve reproducibility. These are useful refinements to a largely stable study. The gains are tempered by the newly malformed masking sentence and the unreconciled Figure 5 grid description, supporting a limited overall improvement.
